issues.description: The source needs a manually clean-SIC s1 table and prepared eas2/calls2/cto3 tables; only a gvkey/datadate identifier list is packaged. The datasheet names PSZ_PythonJAR.py, which is absent from the extracted inventory. These prepared outputs remain the primary route instead of independently recreating text extraction; their contracts remain unknown.

Two direct Part 4 reads have no producer in the supplied source: main.d_prelimsample_a and main.mhhi_merge3. Their exact source/producer and field contracts remain unresolved. Known same-data library and staging routes are recorded separately as supported path setup.

Two Stata input contracts remain unresolved: mean_io is consumed but has no supplied producer, and the case/name mapping from SAS FC_ind to Stata fc_ind is not established by the supplied export instructions. Do not invent or calculate either contract.

The Top-5 branch starts from ownershipper built from main.s34 and immediately sorts by id1. The supplied source derives id1 later on ownershipper2, not on the ownershipper input used by this branch; the exact one-row S34 schema also has no id1. The intended input/key mapping is unresolved and must not be invented.

Known generated members use different SAS librefs or need local staging: map comp.funda to the exact COMP.FUNDA candidate, route share1 loop outputs to the same members later read through covar, route the generated WORK.firms table to main.firms, and stage Part 1/3 outputs under main.hhi_compustat/main.pszsample. These are supported same-data path/staging tasks; verify the main.pszsample gvkey/datacqtr join fields while configuring paths.

The mixed source has direct path and name mismatches with source-supported corrections: SAS exports pszsample.dta while Stata loads pszsample1.dta; Stata generates roa_a but filters roa; SAS produces stdev and firmoverlap while the rename tuple uses stddev and separate firm/overlap tokens; the SAS-produced std_ind_sale is entered as std_ind_sal. These corrections are proposed in a working copy and do not depend on the separate unresolved mean_io/FC_ind contracts.

evidence.description: The datasheet orders the supplied workflow through Compustat, IBES, local merge, Thomson ownership, and Stata variable calculation.
evidence.quote:
We describe these steps in detail in section 3 of the paper and summarize them below. The steps outlined
below follow the sequence of the steps summarized in the program PSZ_SAScodeJAR.sas.
    1. COMPUSTAT: Collect and clean data required to calculate control variables from Compustat.
       To be included in the sample, we require non-missing total assets and SIC codes. Given the
       importance of industry identification to our study, we download SIC codes from Compustat and
       clean/backfill SIC codes manually to ensure we have an accurate and complete sample. This step
       was performed using batch queries to the WRDS servers in SAS.
    2. IBES: Download and clean IBES data, which we use to calculate our analyst following variable
       and the management forecast variable. This step was performed using batch queries to the WRDS
       servers in SAS.
    3. MERGE (SAS): Merge the datasets from Steps 1,2, and 3 with disclosure measures that were
       scraped from EDGAR to get the primary sample of disclosure and control variables. We gather
       the data required to calculate the revenue guidance and customer-specific disclosure variables,
       as well as data for the CTO variable from SEC EDGAR filings and the S&P Global conference
       call dataset. This step was performed locally, in SAS.
    4. THOMSON: Calculate institutional ownership variables and common ownership measures using
       data from the Thomson Reuters 13F database. This step was performed locally in SAS.

review_notes: This assessment covers the full supplied mixed SAS/Stata workflow and all 38 frozen dependencies; the package contains no regression driver, and no analysis-only bypass is evidenced.
